summary: Refactored mcp-server/src/schema/enums.ts: all 4 Zod enums (ProjectStatus, WorkPackageStatus, PipelineStatus, BlockerType) now derive VALUES from shared/workflow-manifest.json at module-load time. ARCHIVED preserved as local extension to ProjectStatus. CommentPriority remains hardcoded (not a spec-level construct). Narrow union types preserved via `as unknown as [...]` tuple assertions since TypeScript widens JSON array imports to string[].

Refactored mcp-server/src/utils/constants.ts: AGENT_ROLES derived from manifest roles[].name, ORCHESTRATING_ROLES from roles with orchestrating=true, SPEC_VERSION from manifest spec_version. New ROLE_IDS map (role name → role ID) exported. AgentRole and OrchestratingRole union types defined explicitly as they cannot be inferred from widened JSON imports. All existing exports preserve their names and semantics.

Key technical finding: TypeScript module: Node16 does not support `with { type: 'json' }` import attributes; plain resolveJsonModule import used instead. Also, TypeScript widens JSON string arrays to string[], preventing literal type inference — explicit type annotations required for type narrowness.
Build (npm run build) succeeds. All 1433 tests pass.

comments.note: TypeScript module:Node16 restricts JSON import syntax — `with { type: 'json' }` is unsupported; `resolveJsonModule` plain imports are the only option. If the project ever upgrades to `module: NodeNext`, JSON imports with assertions would become available and could simplify the type narrowing pattern.

TypeScript widening of JSON arrays (string[] instead of tuple with literals) forces explicit type annotations for enum narrowness. A future alternative: define a Zod schema for the manifest and parse it once at startup to recover narrow types. This would also add runtime validation that the manifest matches the expected shape.

summary: All 5 acceptance criteria are technically met: build passes, 1433 tests pass (via Vitest), all 4 Zod enums derive values from the manifest, ROLE_IDS/SPEC_VERSION are exported, and union types are narrow. However, a regression was discovered: the compiled dist/index.js fails to start on Node.js 22+ when invoked directly via `node`. Both modified files (enums.js, constants.js) emit bare `import from '...workflow-manifest.json'` without the required `with { type: 'json' }` attribute. This is the only path broken — VS Code deployment via `tsx src/index.ts` is unaffected. The orchestrator production path (`orchestrator/src/config.py` line 338: `mcp_server_cmd: list[str] = ['node', str(mcp_server_script)]`) is broken. Before this WP, no files in dist imported JSON, so this is a newly introduced regression.

comments.note: REGRESSION: `node dist/index.js` fails with `ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING` on Node.js 22+ (tested on v25.8.1). Both `dist/schema/enums.js` and `dist/utils/constants.js` emit `import workflowManifest from '../../../shared/workflow-manifest.json'` without `with { type: 'json' }`. Node.js ESM requires this attribute for JSON file imports. VS Code deployment (tsx src/index.ts via .mcp.json) is unaffected. The orchestrator (`orchestrator/src/config.py` line 338: `["node", str(mcp_server_script)]`) is broken. This was NOT a pre-existing issue — before this WP, no files in dist imported JSON. FIX: Replace the static import in both `enums.ts` and `constants.ts` with a `createRequire` pattern: `import { createRequire } from 'module'; const _require = createRequire(import.meta.url); const workflowManifest = _require('../../../shared/workflow-manifest.json') as typeof import('../../../shared/workflow-manifest.json');`. Alternative: upgrade tsconfig to `module: NodeNext` (which supports `with { type: 'json' }` syntax) but this is a larger change. The `createRequire` approach is the smallest, lowest-risk fix.

Tuple type assertions (`as unknown as ['READY', 'IN_PROGRESS', ...]`) in enums.ts are compile-time only. If the manifest's `statuses` arrays are reordered or values renamed, TypeScript will NOT catch the mismatch — the Zod enum gets the runtime values, but the inferred type annotation stays hardcoded. This is acceptable per the developer's design choice, but a future improvement would be to parse the manifest with a Zod schema to get narrow inferred types dynamically.

The `AgentRole` and `OrchestratingRole` union types in constants.ts are hardcoded as TypeScript literal unions (required due to JSON import widening). If a role is added to the manifest but not to both the union type AND the manifest file, TypeScript will not catch the drift. The existing test coverage (work-package.test.ts verifying all non-orchestrating AGENT_ROLES appear in CLAIMABLE_ROLES) provides partial protection, but a dedicated unit test that asserts `AGENT_ROLES.length === AgentRole union member count` would be more explicit.

The compiled output no longer emits bare JSON imports, fixing ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING on Node.js 22+. All module behavior, types, and test assertions are unchanged. summary: Code review PASS. Both modified files (enums.ts and constants.ts) are clean, well-structured, and correctly implement manifest-derived constants. The createRequire pattern is the appropriate solution for the Node.js 22+ ESM+JSON constraint and the dist output confirms no bare JSON ESM imports remain. All acceptance criteria are met. Three non-blocking observations recorded (see comments).

comments.note: ROLE_IDS is exported from constants.ts but has no consumers yet in the TypeScript mcp-server codebase. The orchestrator has a parallel Python derivation at orchestrator/src/config.py:115 (`ROLE_IDS = {r['name']: r['id'] for r in _roles}`). These two will naturally diverge if roles change. A future improvement: emit a generated JSON artifact from the MCP server build step that the orchestrator (and any other consumers) import, eliminating the duplicate derivation.

No dedicated unit tests for the manifest-derivation path of the new ROLE_IDS map. Existing tests exercise AGENT_ROLES and SPEC_VERSION indirectly, but a direct assertion (expect(AGENT_ROLES).toHaveLength(9), expect(ROLE_IDS['Project Manager']).toBe('pm')) would catch manifest path resolution failure or corruption at test time rather than at runtime.

The hardcoded AgentRole and OrchestratingRole union types in constants.ts create a manual synchronization requirement with the manifest roles[].name array. This is a known, acceptable limitation given TypeScript's JSON import widening behavior (documented in the file's block comment). The existing work-package.test.ts check (non-orchestrating AGENT_ROLES appear in CLAIMABLE_ROLES) provides one layer of protection. No action required — recording for future awareness.
